2-carboxamides with Allenes via C−H Bond Activation
Wei Zhou, Xiaohan Zhu, Fen Wang,* and Xingwei Li*
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2025, 27, 12530−12535

ABSTRACT: Reported herein is regiodivergent oxidative annula-
tion of 2-indolylcarboxamides with benzyl allenes via C−H bond
activation of the indole ring via the formation of a π-allyl
intermediate. The regioselectivity is reaction-condition-dependent,
selectively afording the [4 + 1]- or [4 + 3]-annulated product as a
result of functionalization of the proximal or distal allylic site,
respectively.
A<sup>llenes</sup> <sup>are</sup> <sup>fundamentally</sup> <sup>important</sup> <sup>unsaturated</sup> <sup>reagents</sup>in contemporary organic synthesis, and they have found
extensive applications in the fabrication of valuable synthetic
scafolds and bioactive compounds.<sup>1</sup> Allenes have particularly
emerged as versatile coupling partners in metal-catalyzed C−H
bond activation and functionalization reactions of arenes. Their
synthetic value is ascribed to the high reactivity and versatile
reaction patterns during their interactions with diverse
transition metals. Nevertheless, control of the regio- and
chemoselectivities remains a significant challenge that may
deter the use of allenes in metal-catalyzed C−H functionaliza-
tion in comparison to other π systems, such as alkenes and
alkynes.<sup>2</sup> Nevertheless, notable progress has been made toward
addressing the selectivity of allenes by unraveling their unique
reactivities in C−H activation reactions (Scheme 1). Krische
and co-workers disclosed the first iridium-catalyzed C−H
functionalization with allenes in 2009.<sup>3</sup> This chemistry was

and others.<sup>10</sup>

allene chemistry (Scheme 1a). The migratory insertion of R−

and [3 + 3]-<sup>15</sup>

Despite the progress, the reactivity and selectivity of the allyl
species C need further exploration given the fact that the
annulated products are predominantly limited to stable five-
and six-membered rings. We reasoned that, in the case of the
reaction of a five-membered heterocycle (such as indole), the
C−H activation and allene insertion produces an analogous
allyl intermediate C′ (Scheme 1b). The subsequent cyclization
by engaging proximal allyl carbon afords a commonly
encountered
product. However, this product is
thermodynamically unstable due to the inherent ring strain in a
five−five ring fusion.<sup>16</sup> The alternative
annulation
product has been rarely explored,<sup>17</sup> but the formation of a less
strained seven-membered ring is thermodynamically favorable.
By leveraging the reaction conditions, we aimed to address the
regioselectivity of such annulation reactions via allyl inter-
mediates under simple condition control. We now report
oxidant-dependent, chemoselective, and regiodivergent [4 + 1]
and [4 + 3] annulations between 2-indolylcarboxymides and
benzyl allenes under rhodium catalysis (Scheme 1c).
